      "arc_fill_between_parallel_diagonal_stroke_segments": {
        "id": "arc_fill_between_parallel_diagonal_stroke_segments",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Fill between parallel diagonal stroke segments",
        "content": "For ARC grids with background 8 and sparse same-color diagonal strokes on lines r+c=s, apply this rule only when that parallel-diagonal structure is present. Split each line into maximal contiguous segments. Represent each segment by its s value and its endpoint interval in v=r-c. For each integer v, find the segments whose intervals contain v, sort them by s, and fill background-8 cells strictly between each consecutive pair with color 2. Preserve all input strokes. This rule matched demonstrations with source colors 4 and 6 and solved a test with source color 7.",

      "arc_color1_color6_boundary_marking": {
        "id": "arc_color1_color6_boundary_marking",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Color-1/color-6 boundary marking with color 7",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated setup—background 8, color-1 shapes, and a color-6 marker at the upper-right, with output color 7—first check whether the color-1 structure forms a full-height divider. In the non-separating cases (demos 2 and 3 and the solved test), preserve all 1 and 6 cells; recolor to 7 the accessible outer-frame 8 cells and the one-cell 8-neighbor exterior around color-1 components connected to the grid boundary. Leave unrelated interior 8 cells and isolated interior 1 objects unchanged. Distinct divider exception: when a full-height 1 divider separates the 6-side region, keep the divider, clear objects on the opposite side as shown in the demo, and fill the 6-side region with 7. Treat this as a narrow pattern-specific rule; verify the structure against examples before applying, and do not generalize it to unrelated grids.",

      "arc_components_into_matching_bands": {
        "id": "arc_components_into_matching_bands",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Transfer components into matching horizontal bands (general, v2)",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform-background upper workspace containing colored shapes and lower horizontal bands with distinct interior-fill and side-marker colors, process each upper-workspace foreground 4-connected component independently—even when different colors together form one visual motif. Match a component to a lower band when the component's color equals that band's interior-fill color. Project only that component's mask into the matching band at the same columns, bottom-align its bounding box within the band's height, and recolor its cells to the band's side-marker/border color. Leave all other cells in the component's bounding box as the band's fill color, preserve the band and unrelated cells, and clear the original foreground components from the upper workspace. Different colors within one motif can therefore populate different bands. Do not treat a whole multicolor template as one object or recolor its full bounding box. This rule was validated by two demonstrations and a correct solution for task-7c173794; an initial whole-template recoloring guess was incorrect.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},

      "arc_marker_guided_chebyshev_region_layers": {
        "id": "arc_marker_guided_chebyshev_region_layers",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Marker-guided coloring of barrier-separated regions with 8-neighbor layers",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background partitioned by line barriers and marker colors placed at successive inner boundary layers, first confirm this structure from the examples. Preserve barrier cells. Treat each 4-connected free region independently, find its boundary cells (adjacent by king move to a barrier or the grid exterior), and compute inward distance layers using 8-neighbor/king-move propagation within that region. Use the marker colors at successive depths as a cyclic color sequence for the layers, preserving any marker cells if the examples require it. A 4-neighbor BFS layer fill failed on the irregular region in task-9a643f12; the 8-neighbor layer version solved it. Apply only when examples confirm this rule, not as a general rule for arbitrary regions.",
        "path": "general",

      "arc_repack_solid_and_hollow_square_tiles": {
        "id": "arc_repack_solid_and_hollow_square_tiles",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Repack solid and hollow square tiles into sorted columns",
        "content": "For ARC grids containing repeated same-sized solid and hollow square tiles on a background, first verify the tile dimensions and that the objects separate into solid and hollow categories. Preserve each tile's cell pattern and color. Sort each category independently by its original top-to-bottom position. Build the output with hollow tiles in the left column and solid tiles in the right column, one tile per tile-height band; align category items by their sorted index and pad any missing tile with background. Infer output dimensions from the number of bands needed by the longer category. Apply only when the demonstrated structure fits.",

      "arc_quadrant_stencil_fill_and_expand": {
        "id": "arc_quadrant_stencil_fill_and_expand",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Fill and expand a bottom-right quadrant stencil from bottom-left data",
        "content": "For ARC inputs visibly divided into equal quadrants, consider whether the bottom-right quadrant is a repeating stencil whose zero cells are filled using the bottom-left quadrant. Confirm this structure against demonstrations before applying. In the demonstrated solid-data case, the bottom-left quadrant is a single solid color: tile the bottom-right pattern with its zero cells filled by that color, then crop to height equal to the count of nonzero cells in the top-left quadrant and width equal to the count of nonzero cells in the top-right quadrant. In the demonstrated varying-data case, bottom-left values supply fill colors for repeated bottom-right stencil tiles, producing an expanded output (the 8x8-to-16x16 example). A solved test had 16 ones in the top-left, 4 fives in the top-right, solid 9 in the bottom-left, and a 3/0 checkerboard stencil; its output was a 16x4 checkerboard of 3 and 9. One demo with an all-zero bottom-right produced the bottom-left pattern as output, but treat that only as an observed fallback, not a general rule.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},

      "arc_quadrant_mask_expansion": {
        "id": "arc_quadrant_mask_expansion",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Expand bottom-left source through bottom-right mask using top-quadrant counts",
        "content": "For even-sized ARC grids that visibly divide into four equal quadrants, consider this rule only when the upper quadrants encode output dimensions and the lower quadrants form a source-and-mask pair. Count nonzero cells in the top-left quadrant for output height and in the top-right quadrant for output width. Use the bottom-left as the source and the bottom-right as a block mask: expand each source cell into a bottom-right-sized block, preserving nonzero mask colors and replacing mask zeros with that source cell's color, then crop to the counted output dimensions. If the bottom-right is entirely zero, the demonstrated variant is a direct crop of the bottom-left. Confirm the quadrant roles and output dimensions against examples before applying.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},

          "scope": "global",
          "evidence": "Validated by a correct submission on task-b4e6b93d"

      "arc_four_quadrant_count_guided_tile_expansion": {
        "id": "arc_four_quadrant_count_guided_tile_expansion",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Four-quadrant count-guided tile expansion",
        "content": "For even-sized ARC grids that visibly split into four equal quadrants, consider this rule only when the examples support it: the output height is the number of nonzero cells in the upper-left quadrant, and the output width is the number of nonzero cells in the upper-right quadrant. Tile the lower-right quadrant periodically to those dimensions. Preserve its nonzero cells; for each zero at output coordinate (r,c), fill it with the lower-left quadrant cell at (r // q, c // q), where q is the quadrant side length. Validate the quadrant structure, dimensions, and cell mapping against available examples before applying.",

      "arc_marker_count_guided_bar_snake_route": {
        "id": "arc_marker_count_guided_bar_snake_route",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Complete marked bars and route a color-3 snake (general, v1)",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated setup—background 8, straight bars made of colors 1 and 2, and a single color-3 seed—first confirm the bar orientations, order, seed side, and open endpoints from the input and available examples. For horizontal bars approached from the seed side, change their color-1 marker cells to color 2. Route color 3 around each bar on its open side: the demonstrated offset is d = (number of color-1 markers on that bar) + 1, measured both perpendicular to the bar and beyond its endpoint. Alternate sides while proceeding toward the opposite edge, following the demonstrated bends. This was supported by a one-bar demonstration with 4 markers and offset 5, and a correctly solved three-bar test with offsets 2, 3, and 3 from the seed side. Treat the route rule as pattern-specific; do not infer a fixed route or apply it unless the geometry and examples support it.",
        "path": "general",

      "arc_framed_row_major_object_stacking": {
        "id": "arc_framed_row_major_object_stacking",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Stack row-major objects from a framed workspace",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated structure, with background 8, a color-1 top frame, a color-2 left frame, and payload made of separated 2-row-high colored objects, read objects row-major (top to bottom, left to right), preserve each object's pattern, and stack them vertically. Use a canvas as wide as the widest object, centering narrower objects with 8-padding. Confirm the frame and payload layout before applying; do not generalize to other frames or object shapes without evidence.",
        "path": "general",

      "arc_scale_and_mirror_a_quadrant_template_around_color_2_squares": {
        "id": "arc_scale_and_mirror_a_quadrant_template_around_color_2_squares",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Scale and mirror a quadrant template around color-2 squares",
        "content": "For a grid divided by a color-1 cross, when the top-left quadrant contains a motif with a 2x2 color-2 core and the other quadrants contain square color-2 seeds, use the top-left motif as a template. Scale each motif component by target_side/2 around the core and orient it to the destination quadrant: horizontal reflection in the top-right, vertical reflection in the bottom-left, and 180-degree rotation in the bottom-right. Preserve the source quadrant and cross. Apply only when demonstrations support this structure. This rule was validated on two demos (target sides 1-4) and a correct test with target sides 1, 2, and 3.",
        "path": "arc_grid_transformations",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "source": "Continual-ARC demonstrated task-e5f49133",
          "validation": "two demos and correct submission"

      "arc_color2_connector_component_assembly": {
        "id": "arc_color2_connector_component_assembly",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Assemble components by matching color-2 connectors",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated connector-assembly pattern, first verify that colored pieces are rigid components accompanied by color-2 connector cells. Identify each component and record the coordinates of its adjacent color-2 markers; preserve each piece's orientation. In the demonstrated examples, keep the solid color-4 component as the anchor. Find translations that make connector-marker sets from different pieces overlap, using alignments of at least two markers as strong candidates. Assemble a connected chain while favoring complete one-to-one pairing of all connector markers and avoiding overlaps between colored piece cells. Preserve the piece colors and marker cells in the output, and validate the resulting placements and grid dimensions. Treat the anchor, chain structure, and matching rule as specific to grids that visibly support this pattern; do not generalize to unrelated marker layouts.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global"

        "created_at": "2026-09-28T09:26:17.257Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T09:26:17.257Z",

      "arc_masked_canvas_fill_from_object_palette": {
        "id": "arc_masked_canvas_fill_from_object_palette",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Fill a masked canvas from palette objects",
        "content": "For ARC grids where one panel is a canvas containing a base color and mask cells, and a separate palette panel has that mask color as its background, consider replacing the canvas mask cells with foreground patterns copied from palette objects. Confirm the panel roles and color relationship from the input and demonstrations; do not assume a particular color or panel orientation. Treat each palette object as its connected non-background pattern, preserving all internal marker colors. Partition or tile these patterns to cover the mask exactly, using object dimensions, geometry, and area conservation to infer placement. Preserve all base-color canvas cells. Validate that every mask cell is covered and that copied patterns retain their shapes and colors. Verified example: a 15×7 canvas with base color 4 and 41 mask cells of color 7 was filled using palette objects 1 (2×5), 6 (6×2), 2 (2×2), two 8 (1×4), 3 (3×2), and 0 (singleton).",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global",
          "evidence": "Three demonstrations and one correct submission"
        },

        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T10:20:12.649Z",

      "arc_single_vertical_marker_corner_repacking": {
        "id": "arc_single_vertical_marker_corner_repacking",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Single vertical marker sends off-axis patterns to edge corners",
        "content": "For a color-1 grid with a single vertical color-2 marker on the top or bottom edge and a color-7 pattern crossing its column, first confirm the structure. Preserve color-7 cells on the marker column. Extend color 2 from the edge marker along that column through blanks until the first color-7 cell is encountered; preserve any color-7 cells on the axis. Split the off-axis color-7 cells into left and right patterns and translate each pattern rigidly to its corresponding corner on the marker's edge (top-left and top-right for a top marker; bottom-left and bottom-right for a bottom marker), retaining each pattern's cell arrangement. This rule is supported by a bottom-marker demonstration and a correctly submitted top-marker test. Do not generalize to cases with multiple markers based on this evidence.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global"

        "source": "refine",
        "created_at": "2026-09-28T10:50:46.712Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T10:50:46.712Z",

      "arc_framed_piece_order_rotate_and_stack": {
        "id": "arc_framed_piece_order_rotate_and_stack",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Order, rotate, and stack pieces from a color-1/color-2 frame",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated layout, identify the color-8 background, color-1/color-2 top-and-left frame, and the separated foreground pieces inside the frame. Treat each piece as a connected non-background object, excluding frame cells. Order pieces row-major when the top frame is color 1 and the left frame is color 2; order column-major when the top is color 2 and the left is color 1. Rotate any tall piece 90 degrees counterclockwise so its long side is horizontal. Stack pieces vertically in the inferred order, centering each in a canvas whose width is the largest resulting piece width and padding with background 8. Before applying, verify the frame orientation, object separation/connectivity, background, and ordering against the examples; preserve each piece's cell pattern and colors.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global",
          "evidence": "Two demonstrations and a correct test submission"
        },
        "source": "refine",
        "created_at": "2026-09-28T13:06:30.067Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T13:06:30.067Z",
        "version": 1

      "arc_sort_and_repack_hollow_frames_and_solid_blocks": {
        "id": "arc_sort_and_repack_hollow_frames_and_solid_blocks",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Sort and repack hollow frames and solid blocks",
        "content": "For ARC grids containing scattered 4×4 hollow square frames and solid square blocks, first verify that these are the two object classes and that their cell patterns and dimensions match. Extract the objects, sort each class independently by top-to-bottom position in the input, and arrange one 4×4 tile per row in a two-column output: hollow frames on the left and solid blocks on the right. Preserve each object's color and pattern, including zero interiors in frames. If the columns contain different numbers of objects, pad the shorter column with 4×4 zeros. Evidence: a demonstration with frames 3,9 and solid blocks 1,8,5 produced a 12×8 output; a test with frames 8,2,9 and solid blocks 1,3,4,7 produced a 16×8 output and was confirmed correct. Caution: verify both object classes and their top-to-bottom orders before applying; do not generalize to different tile sizes or layouts without evidence.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global"
        },
        "source": "refine",
        "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:26:11.090Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:26:11.090Z",
        "version": 1

      "arc_two_lane_strip_compaction": {
        "id": "arc_two_lane_strip_compaction",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Compact framed two-lane strips by rotating and stacking chunks",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a color-8 background, color-1/color-2 guide borders, and separated vertical strips two cells wide, first verify the guide and strip structure. If the guide orientation is swapped, transpose the grid to canonicalize it to color 2 on top and color 1 on the left. Remove the guide border and identify the vertical chunks in the two strips. Process chunks top-to-bottom in the left strip, then top-to-bottom in the right strip. Rotate each chunk 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically concatenate the results without gaps. Center each rotated chunk horizontally in a color-8 output whose width is the maximum chunk height. Preserve every cell color, including marker cells. Evidence: one demo pair and a correctly solved transposed test instance; confirm the structure before applying.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global"
        },
        "source": "refine",
        "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:32:18.414Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:32:18.414Z",
        "version": 1
      },
      "arc_components_into_matching_trays": {
        "id": "arc_components_into_matching_trays",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Transfer components into matching-color trays",
        "content": "For ARC grids with an upper workspace containing colored components and lower horizontal trays with uniform interior-fill colors and distinct side-rail colors, first verify the layout and component/tray color matches. Route each upper-workspace foreground 4-connected component independently to the tray whose interior fill matches the component’s original color. Preserve the component’s shape and columns, bottom-align it within the tray, and recolor its cells to that tray’s side-rail color. Components of different colors within a motif route separately. Clear the source components to the upper workspace background; preserve tray cells not occupied by transferred components and all unrelated grid regions. Validate tray capacity, component placement, and recoloring before applying.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},
        "metadata": {
          "scope": "global"
        },
        "source": "refine",
        "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:55:55.052Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:55:55.052Z",
        "version": 1
      },
      "arc_touching_color_chain_to_column": {
        "id": "arc_touching_color_chain_to_column",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Flatten a touching chain of colored components into a column",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background and a visibly single chain of differently colored monochrome 4-connected components, transform the chain into a one-column output. Read components in chain order starting from the upper-left endpoint, and repeat each component’s color once per cell in that component. The demonstrated example had counts 7×3, 5×5, 6×5, 8×4, 9×5; the solved test had 8×2, 9×3, 5×6, 1×6, 8×3, 9×5. Apply only when the single touching-chain structure and endpoint/order are supported; count each component’s cells and verify the output height equals the total foreground-cell count.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},

          "scope": "global",
          "task_id": "task-b8158d8c"
        },

      "arc_parallel_stroke_resize_to_color8_reference": {
        "id": "arc_parallel_stroke_resize_to_color8_reference",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Resize parallel strokes to a color-8 reference length",
        "content": "For ARC grids matching the demonstrated pattern, use a straight color-8 stroke as the reference length and resize other straight strokes parallel to it to that length, preserving each resized stroke's endpoint with the greatest row coordinate. Confirm that the strokes share the same orientation, identify the full reference stroke and its length, and verify which colored strokes are eligible before transforming. The demonstrations include diagonal strokes and vertical strokes; do not infer that unrelated or nonparallel objects should be changed.",

      "arc_reorder_color6_panels_by_edge_occupancy": {
        "id": "arc_reorder_color6_panels_by_edge_occupancy",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Reorder color-6-separated panels by matching edge occupancy",
        "content": "For ARC grids with background 7 partitioned by color-6 lines into equal square panels, consider whether the panels must be reordered into a single chain. Apply this rule only when the panel structure and demonstrations support it. For each panel, record binary foreground/background occupancy profiles along all four edges; match adjoining panels by these profiles, regardless of foreground color. Find an ordering that gives blank outer-facing start/end edges when supported by the examples. Preserve every panel's cells, colors, and orientation, and retain color-6 separators between panels. The demonstrated cases included horizontal, vertical, and 2×2 panel layouts; the solved test chained bottom panel → middle panel → top panel. Verify extracted panel boundaries, edge profiles, chain order, output orientation, and separator placement before submitting; do not infer this rule from color-6 lines alone.",
        "path": "general",
        "scope": "global",
        "reference": {},
        "arguments": {},

        },
        "source": "refine",

        "updated_at": "2026-09-28T17:58:22.196Z",
        "version": 1

      "arc_matching_motif_to_solid_panel": {
        "id": "arc_matching_motif_to_solid_panel",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: Pattern solid panels using matching-color motifs",
        "content": "For ARC grids with solid 5×5 color panels separated by one-cell background gutters and an outer border, plus matching 3×3 motifs made of panel colors on the same background, use each color's motif to pattern its corresponding panel. Replace the center 3×3 cells of each panel with the background color wherever the matching motif contains that panel's color; leave the panel color in the other center cells. Preserve the panel arrangement, gutters, and border. First verify the panel and motif dimensions, background color, and color correspondence.
